candidateArtifact.completeText:
# LUMINAiRY profile candidate

Name: Hannah Fry
Role: Keeper of the Explanation

About: Fry’s contribution—recognized by the 2026 Leelavati Prize for increasing public awareness of mathematics—is making the mathematics inside automated decisions visible enough for ordinary people to question. In Hello World, she asks who should decide a criminal case: a person or an algorithm. The point is not that one is automatically fairer; it is that the trade-offs matter when a system shapes healthcare, justice or other consequential choices. LAiDIES calls her Keeper of the Explanation because she turns a hidden system into questions a reader can use: What is it optimizing? What does it miss? Who carries the consequence?

Lesson: Make an invisible technical system understandable by showing where it touches ordinary decisions.

Image: /assets/mavens/y2k-stained-glass-v4-dark-sapphire/hannah-fry-y2k-stained-glass.png

- listen: Listen to The Rest Is Science — https://therestis.com/science
- listen: Listen to Google DeepMind: The Podcast — https://deepmind.google/the-podcast/
- watch: Watch Hannah Fry on YouTube — https://www.youtube.com/@fryrsquared
- follow: Follow Hannah Fry on Instagram — https://www.instagram.com/fryrsquared/
- follow: Follow Hannah Fry on X — https://x.com/FryRsquared

Freshness: Role and destinations checked 2 Sep 2026

facts.sourceExcerpt: she lifts the lid on their inner workings, demonstrates their power, exposes their limitations, and examines whether they really are an improvement on the humans they are replacing.

transfer.scenario: A reader's mortgage application is declined by her bank's automated credit-scoring model, with no human explanation offered.
transfer.question: Do the profile's closing questions — What is it optimizing? What does it miss? Who carries the consequence? — give her real traction on this new automated decision?
transfer.answer: Yes. 'What is it optimizing?' surfaces that the model maximizes predicted repayment probability, not her actual circumstances. 'What does it miss?' surfaces thin credit files, recent income changes, or informal savings the model never sees. 'Who carries the consequence?' identifies that she, not the bank, bears the cost of a false negative — which motivates asking for a manual review or the specific decline reasons.
transfer.assessment: The questions transfer cleanly to an unfamiliar consequential automated decision without needing the Fry example; they are a genuine reusable tool, not decorative rhetoric. Transfer test passes.

issues.finding: The word 'optimizing' is the one abstraction a complete beginner might stumble on; it is immediately anchored by the two companion questions and by concrete domains (healthcare, justice), so it does not block comprehension and does not rise to material.
issues.artifactExcerpt: What is it optimizing? What does it miss? Who carries the consequence?

learningDisposition.rationale: The candidate passes with zero material issues, avoids all registered failure families (no glossary accumulation, no title-only biography, no award-list substitution, no promotional-claim inheritance from publisher copy), and the negative control behaved as expected. No new reusable defect pattern or evidence gap was uncovered worth registering.

judgment.summary: PASS. The candidate About earns the celebration the incumbent could not: a prize-recognized distinctive contribution (2026 Leelavati, verified against the Cambridge primary source), one concrete example from Hello World (verbatim in Penguin copy, with publisher-copy limits respected — the artifact deliberately does not inherit Penguin's claim that algorithms are less error-prone), a real reader consequence, and three closing questions that independently transfer to new automated decisions such as credit scoring. All seven locked fields including byte-identical links are preserved; 98 words fits the shared card; voice is warm third-person with no founder voice, jargon, or generic inspirational close. One minor, non-blocking note on the word 'optimizing'. The incumbent title-only control independently earns REJECT as expected.

limitations: AI editorial assessment; no observed human comprehension is claimed.
Penguin is publisher copy. It supports the book example and scope, not independent evaluation.
This review does not sign, integrate or publish the profile.
